sc: Jaundice in the first 24 h, mother group O, positive Coombs → Haemolytic disease of the newborn
Membranes ruptured > 18 h, poor suck and low temperature on day 2 → Neonatal sepsis: septic screen, ampicillin + gentamicin
Early stop of breastfeeding, diluted bottle feeds, repeated diarrhoea → Feeding–infection cycle (malnutrition)
f: Day of onset · stool and urine colour · feeding · blood groups · siblings with jaundice · drugs, fava (G6PD)
Rupture of membranes, maternal fever · prematurity · poor suck, lethargy, temperature, fits
Feeding history · diarrhoea, cough, TB contact · oedema onset · appetite · HIV · immunization
Frequency, blood, duration · vomiting · drinking and passing urine · feeding · contacts, water source
Jaundice: total + direct bilirubin, groups, Coombs, CBC, retics · sepsis: blood culture, CBC, CRP, LP
Classify dehydration → Plan A, B or C · bloody diarrhoea: ciprofloxacin
trap: Jaundice in the first day is never physiological · pale stools with jaundice at 3 weeks = biliary atresia: urgent · a septic newborn is often hypothermic
